title: Tenant-aware adaptive sampling sidecar for inference KPIs (Prometheus/OTel)
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a small, language-agnostic sidecar to run adaptive, tenant-aware sampling and lightweight pre-aggregation for inference KPIs (Prometheus/OTel). The sidecar will sit in front of the existing OTLP ingest pipeline on Dedicated and Private nodes to reduce cardinality and control cost while preserving SLO-relevant signals. It should support deterministic sampling, dynamic rate changes driven by SLO deviation signals, and enrichment tags (model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, cold_start) for downstream rollups.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar accepts OTLP/HTTP and OTLP/gRPC metrics and exports to the existing telemetry gateway without schema changes
Deterministic sampling policy implemented: hash(tenant, route, request_id_prefix) to ensure reproducible samples
Adaptive controller adjusts sampling rate per-tenant and per-route based on a configurable SLO deviation metric (latency/error) and can be toggled via config/flag
Preserves a low-overhead representative set of latency histograms and token-count counters for each sampled request
Integration tests demonstrating end-to-end: sidecar -> telemetry-gateway -> prometheus/long-term storage with correct labels
CPU/memory overhead for sidecar stays within 80MB and 2% CPU under typical Dedicated node load (benchmarks included)
Dashboard (Grafana) panels show sampled vs unsampled latency curves and sampling rate over time for a test tenant
implementation_notes: Approach: lightweight Rust sidecar using opentelemetry-proto for OTLP ingestion. Two paths: (1) fast path for non-sampled counters (aggregate and forward); (2) sampled-span path for histogram and trace hooks. Use deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by tenant+route to keep representative histograms. Adaptive controller runs a sliding-window SLO detector (p99 latency breach) and increases sample rate for affected routes. Backpressure: apply token-bucket queue with async drain to avoid blocking inference process. Config: per-tenant policy file (s3/kv) with defaults and overrides. Feature flag for canary rollout.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Chose OTLP ingestion to avoid dual-encoders; converts prompt/token counters into OTLP metrics at edge.
- Language choice: Rust for memory/cpu efficiency; increases initial dev time but reduces operational overhead.
- Deterministic sampling preserves reproducibility for debugging, but may bias cold-start signals; mitigated by explicit cold_start tag override that forces sampling.
- We will not attempt full trace capture in first iteration; span hooks will emit a lightweight sample reference ID to correlate with traces saved by the tracing pipeline.

rollout_plan: 1) Deploy sidecar as opt-in for Canary tenants via autoscale group. 2) Monitor sampling rate and SLO delta metrics for 72h. 3) Increase tenant rollout in waves (10%, 30%, 60%). 4) Revert path: disable sidecar via placement tag and fall back to gateway. 5) After 4 weeks, flip default to enabled for Dedicated nodes and provide knob for Private installs.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: sampling-rate-by-tenant, sampled_vs_total_latency, sample-coverage-heatmap. Alerts: sample_coverage_drop (>=50% drop sustained 10m), controller_error_rate > 1% 5m. SLO regression alert tied to canary tenants triggers automated rollback.
